subject: Post-call: performance qualification & customer-led load test planning
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@orbitai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: performance qualification & customer-led load test planning

Hi Liam — great run through earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled: 

Summary of perf requirements you outlined on the call:
- 95th-pctl latency target: <= 250ms for synchronous text generation (16k context)
- Sustained throughput target: 120 tokens/sec aggregate across three concurrent clients (burst to 400 tokens/sec okay for short intervals)
- Streaming requirements: server-side keepalive + partial tokens every 100-200ms for UI quality; we should simulate both chunked and unchunked streaming patterns
- Concurrency: you expect up to 70 concurrent streaming sessions during peak window

What we need from you to proceed:
1) Confirm the customer-led test window (suggested: Fri Nov 5 10:00–12:00 PT)
2) Decide whether your team will run Locust (preferred on your side) or run k6 from your infra — we can provide both scripts as references
3) Provide the public egress IPs (or CIDR) that Locust/k6 workers will use so we can add to the allowlist
4) Confirm which dataset/profile to use (prod-representative, ~75% real-world prompt mix)

What Redwood will deliver before the window:
- Test accounts and short-lived API keys scoped to a sandbox model (will expire automatically)
- An attachable k6 streaming probe script and an optional lightweight Node-based streaming probe (attachment: redwood_k6_stream_probe_v1.js)
- IP allowlist template (attachment: ip_allowlist_orbitai.csv) and sample Locust task guidance
- A runbook with canary/fallback play (link in HubSpot and drive doc)

If that all looks good, reply with the confirmed window and your IPs and we'll stand up the test accounts and share credentials via secure note.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@orbitai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance qualification & customer-led load test planning

Thanks Karthik — summary looks accurate and we’re aligned on requirements. A few notes from our side: 

- We intend to run Locust from our CI runners (we prefer Locust for thread-based streaming checks) but we can run your k6 probe as a reference to validate tokenization and timing.
- Proposed window: Fri Nov 5, 10:00–12:00 PT (that works for our ops team)
- Public egress IPs (will originate from our CI pool): 52.34.201.12, 52.34.201.13, 52.34.201.14 (I’ll attach a text file with the list)
- We want one warm-up canary at 09:45PT for quick health checks, then ramp to target over 10 minutes
- Can you confirm token rate limits we should expect on the test account? If there’s soft throttling we need to tune Locust accordingly.

I’ll run the Locust tasks and share the task definition after I adapt the k6 sample you mentioned. Attaching our IP list now.

— Liam
Liam O'Neill
Head of Platform Engineering, OrbitAI
liam.oneill@orbitai.com

Attachments: orbitai_load_ips.txt

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@orbitai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance qualification & customer-led load test planning

Liam — thanks, got the IP list. We’ll add those IPs to the allowlist for the sandbox keys. A few action items I’m completing now: 

- I’ve provisioned scoped test API keys and a short-run sandbox model (notes attached: redwood_test_account_notes.txt). Keys will be shared to you via our secure credential portal 30 minutes before the warm-up.
- Attached is the k6 streaming probe (redwood_k6_stream_probe_v1.js). It supports both chunked and non-chunked streaming patterns and includes a helper to emit partial tokens on an interval to mimic your UI. You can port logic to Locust if you prefer.
- Attached is the IP allowlist template (ip_allowlist_orbitai.csv) — please confirm the CIDR format you want used in your firewall rules.
- Token rate expectations for the sandbox keys: soft limit ≈ 1000 tokens/minute/account with burst headroom; we’ll watch for 429s and surface early. For the production-equivalent paths we’ll test with the same limits but different throttling behavior may apply.

Internal note: Neha, can you prepare the streaming canary and service-side probe so we can execute the 09:45 warm-up? Also include a fallback where we automatically route to the smaller model if we hit sustained 5xx errors.

If that all looks good I’ll schedule the secure key delivery and drop a final runbook link in HubSpot.

— Karthik

Attachments: redwood_k6_stream_probe_v1.js, ip_allowlist_orbitai.csv, redwood_test_account_notes.txt

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: performance qualification & customer-led load test planning

Karthik / Steph — internal checklist and readiness items before keys go out:

- Provisioning: confirm sandbox API keys TTL = 6 hours, scopes restricted to /v1/generate + streaming endpoint only
- Observability: create temporary dashboard for deal HW-4762 with token-level breakdown and per-session latency; add log sampling for 429/5xx at 100% during the window
- Canary: schedule 09:45PT warm-up with 5 lightweight streaming sessions from our side (Node probe) to validate connection keepalives and chunk cadence
- Fallback policy: auto-route to quantized smaller model after 3xx cumulative 5xx within a 60s window; notify ops on slack and escalate to on-call infra if persistent
- Credentials handoff: use secure credential portal link, do not email keys inline
- Contact list: on-call infra — infra-oncall@redwood.com; CS lead — stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

I'll prepare the runbook section for streaming-specific checks and paste the link into HubSpot once keys are scheduled. Karthik — let me know the exact timestamp you plan to deliver the keys and I’ll ensure the canary is ready 10 minutes prior.

— Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@orbitai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Nov 2027 16:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance qualification & customer-led load test planning

All good on our end — confirmed:
- We will run Locust from our CI and reuse the k6 probe as a timing reference.
- Window confirmed: Fri Nov 5, 10:00–12:00 PT with warm-up at 09:45PT.
- Our public egress IPs (final) attached again: 52.34.201.12, 52.34.201.13, 52.34.201.14
- We accept the sandbox token rate guidance; will ramp slowly and not exceed the soft rate during the first 15 minutes. We will provide the Locustfile by 07:00 PT on test day for quick pre-checks.

Thanks for the prompt coordination — looking forward to the run. If anything changes I’ll flag it here.

— Liam

Attachments: orbitai_load_ips.txt
